topics.name: Artificial Intelligence
topics.answer: Artificial Intelligence, or AI, is the field of computer science that builds machines and software able to do tasks that normally need human intelligence, such as understanding language, recognising images, making decisions and learning from experience. Machine learning is one of the main ways AI is achieved.

topics.name: Machine Learning
topics.answer: Machine Learning is a branch of Artificial Intelligence where computers learn patterns from data instead of being given step by step rules. For example, after seeing thousands of emails marked as spam, a machine learning model can learn to spot new spam by itself. The more good data it learns from, the better its predictions usually become.

topics.name: Deep Learning
topics.answer: Deep Learning is a part of machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers, inspired loosely by the human brain. These layers learn increasingly complex features from data, which is why deep learning is used for image recognition, speech recognition and language translation.

topics.name: Python
topics.answer: Python is a popular, beginner-friendly programming language known for its clear and readable syntax. It is used for web development, automation, data science, artificial intelligence and many other things, and it comes with a very large collection of ready-made libraries.

topics.name: Java
topics.answer: Java is a general-purpose, object-oriented programming language designed to run on any device that has a Java Virtual Machine, following the idea of write once, run anywhere. It is widely used for Android apps, enterprise software and large back-end systems.

topics.name: Programming
topics.answer: Programming is the process of writing instructions, called code, that tell a computer what to do. Programmers use languages such as Python, Java or C to build software, websites and apps by breaking problems into small, logical steps.

topics.name: Computer Science
topics.answer: Computer Science is the study of computers and computation. It covers how to design algorithms, write programs, organise data, build hardware and software systems, and apply computing to solve real-world problems.

topics.name: Internet
topics.answer: The Internet is a global network that connects millions of computers and devices so they can exchange information. It carries services such as websites, email, video calls and online banking, using shared rules called protocols such as TCP and IP.

topics.name: Database
topics.answer: A database is an organised collection of data stored so that it can be easily searched, updated and managed. Software called a Database Management System, such as MySQL or PostgreSQL, helps applications store and retrieve that data safely.

topics.name: SQL
topics.answer: SQL, which stands for Structured Query Language, is the standard language used to work with relational databases. With commands such as SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE you can read, add, change and remove data stored in tables.

topics.name: MySQL
topics.answer: MySQL is a free, open-source relational database management system. It stores data in tables and uses SQL to manage it, and it is very popular for websites and web applications.

topics.name: Data Science
topics.answer: Data Science is the practice of collecting, cleaning and analysing data to find useful insights and make predictions. It combines statistics, programming and domain knowledge, and often uses machine learning.

topics.name: Cyber Security
topics.answer: Cyber security is the practice of protecting computers, networks, apps and data from attacks, theft and damage. It includes strong passwords, encryption, firewalls, software updates and awareness of scams such as phishing.

topics.name: Cloud Computing
topics.answer: Cloud computing means using computing resources such as servers, storage and databases over the internet, usually paying only for what you use, instead of owning and maintaining your own hardware. Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud are well-known providers.

topics.name: HTML
topics.answer: HTML, which stands for HyperText Markup Language, is the standard language for creating the structure of web pages. It uses tags to define headings, paragraphs, links, images and other elements that browsers display.

topics.name: CSS
topics.answer: CSS, or Cascading Style Sheets, is the language that controls how HTML elements look on a web page, including colours, fonts, spacing and layout. It lets designers keep the appearance separate from the content.

topics.name: JavaScript
topics.answer: JavaScript is the programming language of the web. It runs in the browser to make pages interactive, for example menus, forms and animations, and with Node.js it can also run on servers. Despite the similar name, it is a different language from Java.

topics.name: Computer Networks
topics.answer: A computer network is a group of connected computers and devices that can share data and resources. Examples range from a home Wi-Fi network to the Internet. Networks rely on devices such as routers and switches and on protocols such as TCP and IP.

topics.name: Operating System
topics.answer: An operating system is the main software that manages a computer's hardware and lets other programs run. It handles memory, files, devices and security. Windows, Linux, macOS and Android are common examples.

topics.name: Software Engineering
topics.answer: Software Engineering is the disciplined approach to designing, building, testing and maintaining software. It follows stages such as requirements, design, coding, testing and maintenance, so that large programs are reliable and easy to improve.
